name: Audio and narration boundary
observations: OpenMontage’s Remotion composer declares @remotion/media ^4.0.484 plus @remotion/captions, but the inspected composer components import Audio from remotion rather than directly from @remotion/media; package scripts render the Explainer composition with Remotion CLI. (remotion-composer/package.json:5-23; remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:1-9)

Explainer exposes an optional audio object with narration and music layers. Narration requires src and optional linear volume. Music adds offsetSeconds, loop, fade-in, and fade-out controls; music defaults to volume 0.1 and is frame-volume-shaped across the whole composition. (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:284-308,884-917)

CinematicRenderer has a separate soundtrack/narration layer and music layer. Both use a shared Soundtrack component with trim-before/after and frame-based fade envelopes; soundtrack defaults to full volume, music to 0.15, with music fades of 2 seconds in and 3 seconds out. (remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:387-437,457-489)

Explainer metadata derives duration from the latest cut end plus one second and uses 30 fps; the root composition defaults to 1920x1080, 30 fps, and an empty audio object. Cinematic metadata derives duration from scene start plus duration and uses 1920x1080 at 30 fps. (remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:123-166; remotion-composer/src/CinematicRenderer.tsx:440-454)

OpenMontage’s AudioMixer is a deterministic FFmpeg tool supporting mix, duck, extract, full_mix, and segmented_music. Its contract distinguishes speech/music/SFX roles, per-track volume, scheduling, fades, ducking envelope timings, LUFS target, and exact full_mix target duration. (tools/audio/audio_mixer.py:26-36,43-61,63-195)

AudioMixer applies source-side fades before adelay, disables amix normalization to preserve caller-set levels, uses loudnorm with a clamped target (default -16 LUFS), and uses an alimiter when loudnorm is skipped. (tools/audio/audio_mixer.py:210-244,246-277,302-361)

Simple ducking treats primary_audio as speech and secondary_audio as music; advanced ducking selects the first speech/primary and first music/secondary track. The default music-during-speech volume is 0.15, with default attack 200 ms and release 500 ms, and speech is mixed without amix normalization. (tools/audio/audio_mixer.py:363-472)

TTS is a capability boundary: TTSSelector discovers all registry tools declaring capability=tts, supports explicit preferred/allowed provider routing, rank-only mode, provider scoring, offline fallback, multilingual controls, timestamps, and output-path propagation. (tools/audio/tts_selector.py:1-6,22-44,46-174,176-255)

The shared HyperFrames audio engine accepts neutral audio_request.json with provider/lang/speed/lines and optional BGM; it writes id-keyed audio_meta.json containing provider/voice, per-line voice paths/durations/words, BGM state, SFX, total voice duration, and non-fatal anomalies. TTS lines are generated concurrently, written under assets/voice/{id}.wav, probed for positive duration, and failed/empty/bad lines are omitted with anomalies. (.agents/skills/hyperframes-media/scripts/audio.mjs:1-40,90-165,260-282)

The HyperFrames provider chain is HeyGen then ElevenLabs then local Kokoro. HeyGen supplies word timestamps in the same call; ElevenLabs and Kokoro require a separate Whisper transcription pass. Provider selection honors explicit choices and rejects unavailable explicit providers. (.agents/skills/hyperframes-media/scripts/lib/tts.mjs:1-15,22-46,48-71,124-209; .agents/skills/hyperframes-media/references/tts.md:7-26)

OpenMontage’s ElevenLabs provider has an optional with_timestamps path that saves an alignment sidecar and word timestamps; its ordinary path returns only audio. Tests require missing alignment to fail loudly and verify PCM output is wrapped as WAV. (tools/audio/elevenlabs_tts.py:74-184,261-357; tests/tools/test_elevenlabs_timestamps.py:27-107)

VideoCompose treats mixed audio as a separate mux input: it can probe/inject silent audio for source clips, replace the final video audio with audio_path, map 0:v and 1:a, encode AAC, and use -shortest. It also accepts narration transcript/script inputs for content-level final review. (tools/video/video_compose.py:121-145,370-434,594-714)

OpenMontage’s source-media review schema requires observed audio technical metadata such as duration, audio codec, sample rate, channels, content/transcript summaries, quality risks, and usable-for implications when user audio is supplied. (schemas/artifacts/source_media_review.schema.json:1-5,15-64,70-82)
The target repository identifies itself as AGPLv3 in its README badge and license section; this analysis does not copy implementation text or assets. (README.md:30,757)

Current MPS MPVE accepts a narration string in VideoRequest and feeds it into storyboard planning, but has no audio asset/provider fields in the request contract. (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:26-68,98-128; MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:9-24)

Current MPS local rendering creates PNG frames and invokes FFmpeg with video-only inputs, returning RenderResult.audio=False. The documented local path is explicitly silent when narration/TTS is unavailable. (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-55,183-210; MPS-git/README.md:104-117)

Current MPS manifests and result payloads record only a boolean audio flag, not audio asset paths, provider/voice identity, word timings, mix settings, loudness, transcript QA, or mux details. (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:203-226; MPS-git/scripts/production_manifest.py:28-73)

MPS tests verify narration text is present in storyboards and verify playable H.264 video/manifest behavior, but do not test generated audio, muxing, ducking, timestamps, captions synchronized to audio, or narration provider selection. (MPS-git/tests/test_hybrid_video.py:14-64; MPS-git/tests/test_production_manifest.py:12-35; MPS-git/tests/test_mpve.py:49-73)
inferences: The practical OpenMontage boundary is staged audio production outside the Remotion visual composition: provider-specific TTS creates line assets and word timing, FFmpeg mixes/ducks/normalizes them, and Remotion or final composition consumes resolved asset paths.

OpenMontage supports two integration styles: pre-mixed external audio muxed by VideoCompose, and independent narration/music layers rendered by Remotion. They are not equivalent: independent layers expose frame-level fades/looping, while AudioMixer supplies speech-aware ducking and loudness control.

Word-level timing is a first-class narration-to-caption bridge, with a fast native-timestamp route and a transcription fallback. A clean MPVE integration should preserve timing as a separate artifact rather than infer captions from the script alone.

OpenMontage’s audio contracts are provider-neutral at the selector/request layer but provider-native at execution, so a clean implementation should keep provider credentials, voice IDs, model IDs, and API-specific controls behind adapters.

MPS currently has a text narration contract but no audio lifecycle; therefore its current audio=false result is honest rather than a failed hidden feature. Adding narration requires changes at request validation, job staging, renderer/muxing, manifest, and QA boundaries.

The target’s ducking tests imply that overlapping scheduled narration must not be attenuated merely because multiple inputs exist; preserving explicit track gain and testing release timing are important behavioral invariants.
unknowns: The inspected target package does not establish whether @remotion/media is imported elsewhere at runtime outside the composer source search; the dependency is declared but the shown audio components use remotion.Audio.

The target source does not, from the inspected files, define one universal schema joining TTS output metadata, audio mixer output, Remotion props, and final QA; the HyperFrames audio_meta shape and Python tool results are separate boundaries.

The exact provider credentials, runtime availability, rate limits, and failure/retry behavior in a deployed OpenMontage installation are environment-dependent; source contracts expose availability checks but do not prove production provider behavior.

MPS has no current choice of narration provider, voice, language, timing mode, audio mix policy, or user consent policy beyond the generic narration string and optional host/provider extension language.
MPS’s existing hosted renderer hook is typed as a video renderer and does not specify whether hosted implementations return or mux audio; this requires an adapter-level contract decision.
contracts: Audio request contract: provide an operation plus track paths/roles and optional volumes, start offsets, fades, ducking parameters, normalization/LUFS target, and output path; full_mix additionally supports exact target duration. (tools/audio/audio_mixer.py:45-195)

TTS selector contract: text is required; provider routing may be automatic, preferred, or allow-listed; rank mode returns provider rankings without generation; generation returns selected provider/tool context on success. (tools/audio/tts_selector.py:46-174,211-255)

Narration timing contract: word entries are normalized to id/text/start/end; native HeyGen timings can be used directly, while ElevenLabs/Kokoro require transcription. (.agents/skills/hyperframes-media/scripts/lib/tts.mjs:74-85,124-209)

Remotion Explainer contract: audio.narration.src is a resolved asset and narration volume defaults to 1; audio.music.src is optional and supports offset, loop, fades, and a volume curve. (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:284-308,884-917)

Final mux contract: if external audio_path exists, VideoCompose maps source video plus external audio, encodes AAC, and uses -shortest; otherwise it preserves source audio. (tools/video/video_compose.py:665-714)

MPS lifecycle contract: MPS submits structured context, MPVE plans/renders, returns artifact and metadata, and MPS resumes written teaching/mastery; fallback-only output is not a genuine video and does not imply mastery. (MPS-git/docs/mpve-integration.md:5-42; MPS-git/skills/mpve/SKILL.md:10-18,30-40)
MPS render contract currently permits a successful silent MP4 and reports audio as a boolean. (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-55,204-210; MPS-git/docs/mpve-report.md:58-67)
mps_gaps: No TTS provider adapter or selector exists in MPS MPVE; narration remains text-only and the local renderer produces no audio stream.
No MPVE request fields exist for narration provider, voice, language, timing/caption mode, music/SFX, audio asset references, or mix policy; only narration text is accepted.
No audio staging step exists between storyboard planning and rendering, so there is no place to generate line audio, transcribe timings, mix/duck tracks, or persist audio metadata.

RenderResult and render.manifest.json expose only audio: boolean; they omit provider, voice/model, paths, duration, loudness target/measurements, ducking, timestamps, transcript comparison, and mux provenance.
The current local renderer cannot attach narration or music and its hosted adapter type does not define audio-capable output semantics.

MPS has no audio-specific QA gates or tests for stream presence when narration is requested, spoken-content fidelity, word timing/caption sync, clipping, LUFS/true peak, ducking envelopes, or silent fallback policy by request mode.
The MPS docs say narration/captions are host/provider extensions but do not define an extension schema, credential boundary, artifact retention policy, or deterministic fallback ordering.
clean_room_recommendations: Define an independent AudioPlan/AudioResult contract for MPVE: requested narration lines and IDs, provider policy, voice/language, optional word timing, music/SFX tracks, mix policy, target loudness, and final artifacts. Keep it distinct from OpenMontage names and implementation structure.

Add an explicit audio stage after storyboard creation and before video render. It should produce durable per-line audio, optional word-timing JSON, a mixed audio asset, and an auditable audio manifest; no provider credentials or API payloads should cross into the visual renderer.

Implement a provider-neutral TTS interface with local deterministic fallback and explicit availability/error states. Require explicit user/host policy before selecting cloud narration, and make silent output an intentional, reported fallback rather than an implicit success when narration was requested.

Choose one clean composition strategy per render: either mux a pre-mixed audio artifact into the MP4, or pass independent narration/music layers to a Remotion-capable renderer. Prefer pre-mixing when speech-aware ducking, LUFS normalization, exact target duration, or SFX are required; reserve independent layers for simple frame-timed audio.

Persist audio provenance in the MPVE manifest: provider/tool, model and voice identifiers, input text hash, output path, duration, format/sample rate/channels, timing artifact, mix settings, loudness target/measurement, and warnings. Avoid recording secrets or raw provider responses.

Add QA gates modeled independently on observed behavior: requested narration must yield an audio stream or a declared fallback; probe duration/codec/channels; compare a transcript artifact against the script; validate word timing monotonicity and caption sync; measure loudness/true peak and clipping; verify music attenuation during speech and release timing.

Extend VideoRequest conservatively with an optional narration policy/object rather than making narration mandatory. Preserve the current silent path for requests without narration, but reject or mark degraded requests when narration is explicitly required and unavailable.

Update MPVE result metadata from a boolean to a structured audio status while retaining a compatibility boolean: requested, generated, mixed, muxed, silent_fallback, provider, artifacts, QA, and errors. Keep MPS pedagogy ownership unchanged and never let audio/provider failure affect mastery state.

Add focused tests before wiring a real provider: provider selection/availability, deterministic local fallback, idempotent artifact naming, missing/empty audio, mux duration preservation, transcript mismatch, word-timing schema, loudness/clipping, and ducking envelope behavior. Use synthetic tones/fixtures for offline tests and no copied OpenMontage source/assets.
